newsitem.title: USA: Mentor sees first half revs up 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mentor sees first half revs up 15 pct.

text.p: Mentor Inc, which makes medical and surgical devices, said Wednesday it expects fiscal 1997 first half revenues to increase 15 percent over the year-earlier $86.1 million.

"First half revenues will probably increase at about the same rate as first quarter revenues," said Christopher Conway, Mentor chairman, in an interview after a presentation to a Dain Bosworth health care conference here.
First quarter revenues rose 15 percent from a year earlier.
Conway said research and development spending this year would total $19 million.
"We spend about nine percent of our revenues on R&D. This year, we'll spend $19 million," he said.
Conway confirmed that $19 million in research and development spending would be eight to nine percent of expected fiscal 1997 revenues.
At nine percent, that projects revenues at $211 million, representing a 19 percent increase over fiscal 1996 revenues of $177.8 million.
Sales of Mentor's plastic surgery products have assumed a larger proportion of total sales, urology products a smaller proportion, and ophthalmology products a constant proportion, Conway said.

"The proportions of sales by the three sectors are likely to stay about the same through the years," he said. "Plastic surgery has been the fastest growing, but when we see some of the ophthalmology products come on line, we'll see their growth rate increase."
